buffers.name: Phosphate
buffers.notes: Very common biological buffer. Incompatible with calcium and magnesium due to high precipitation risk.

buffers.name: Acetate
buffers.notes: Used widely in biochemistry and molecular biology, volatile at high temperatures.

buffers.name: Tris
buffers.notes: Highly temperature dependent (dpKa/dT ~ -0.028/C). Toxic to some cells at high concentrations. Reacts with copper.

buffers.name: HEPES
buffers.notes: Zwitterionic buffer. Excellent for cell culture. Phototoxic when exposed to ambient light due to H2O2 generation.

buffers.name: Bicarbonate
buffers.notes: Key physiological buffer. Undergoes CO2 outgassing in open systems, causing pH drift.

buffers.name: Citrate
buffers.notes: Chelates divalent cations (Ca2+, Mg2+). Useful for antigen retrieval and metal binding.

buffers.name: Glycine
buffers.notes: Used in electrophoresis running buffers. Amino acid buffer.

buffers.name: MES
buffers.notes: Zwitterionic morpholinic buffer. Good for plant and bacterial culture.

buffers.name: MOPS
buffers.notes: Similar to HEPES, morpholinic buffer. Used in RNA gel electrophoresis.

buffers.name: Borate
buffers.notes: Toxic to plants and living cell culture. Forms complexes with cis-diols (e.g. carbohydrates).

buffers.name: Cacodylate
buffers.notes: Contains arsenic. Highly toxic by inhalation/ingestion. Strict disposal protocols required.

buffers.name: PIPES
buffers.notes: Piperazine zwitterionic buffer. Charge starting at -1 because first sulfonate (pKa ~2) is fully ionized at working pH.
